newsitem.title: SWEDEN: SOCCER-SWEDEN BEAT SHAMBOLIC SCOTS 2-1 IN QUALIFIER.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-SWEDEN BEAT SHAMBOLIC SCOTS 2-1 IN QUALIFIER.

text.p: Sweden restored their chances of qualifying for the 1998 World Cup on Wednesday with a comfortable 2-1 victory over a shambolic-looking Scotland.
Sweden's lanky Bologna striker Kennet Andersson was the hero of the evening, scoring each side of the interval as the home team imposed total dominance on Scotland.

Scotland, looking far from the team that heads the World Cup qualifying group four, never got into the game and had to settle for a consolation goal from Blackburn striker Kevin Gallacher from the the visitors' first corner seven minutes from time.
Sweden should have had another when Anderlecht midfielder Per Zetterberg left Scottish keeper Jim Leighton stranded with a floated shot that hit the underside of the bar in the 55th minute.

Sweden's mercurial striker Martin Dahlin made both of Andersson's goals, nodding the ball back in the 43rd minute for Andersson to hammer an unstoppable volley past Leighton to give the Swedes a 1-0 halftime lead.

In the 63rd minute Dahlin slid the ball past a square and stranded Scottish defence for Andersson to slot home a second goal that puts Sweden's World Cup quest firmly back on track and makes Scotland's group lead look somewhat shaky.
Both Sweden and Austria have two games in hand over Scotland, who stay on 14 points, just four ahead of Austria, who beat Estonia 2-0, and five clear of Sweden.
